title: fix(metadata-core): a reorder of an object's fields is a content change, so the designer's publish is no longer dropped (#21790)
body:
Fixes #21790
Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

`ObjectSchema.fields` is a name-keyed map, and the spec declares its traversal order to be the field order. `canonicalize` sorted every map, so a pure reorder of `fields` hashed equal to the published row. `SysMetadataRepository.put` treats an equal hash as a no-op and skipped the write. `promoteDraft` then drained the draft anyway. So the publish answered success, the served object kept the old order, and the draft was gone. That is the card's reproduction. Under the reverse verification below, the new dogfood pin reproduces it: it reads `title, amount, due` back after publishing `due, title, amount`.

## The fix

- **`@objectstack/metadata-core`**: `canonicalize(value, type?)` and `hashSpec(value, type?)` take the metadata type. A per-type table names the maps whose key order is content. Today it has one row, `object` maps to `fields`, and the table's docblock cites the spec text behind it. That map keeps its insertion order in the canonical form. Everything else stays key-order independent: the keys around `fields`, the keys inside each field definition, and every map of every other type. Without a type, the output is byte-identical to before. The table is exported read-only as `orderedMapKeys(type?)`. `InMemoryRepository` and the shared contract suite hash as `ref.type`, and invariant 4 is restated as `item.hash === hashSpec(item.body, item.ref.type)`.
- **`@objectstack/metadata-protocol`**: `SysMetadataRepository` hashes as `ref.type` (in `put`, and in the `rowToItem` fallback for a null checksum). For a type with an ordered map, its no-op short-circuit compares content: it re-hashes the stored body under the current rule rather than trusting the stored stamp. A skipped write returns the stored stamp, which is the version every reader already holds (see H4).
- **`@objectstack/metadata-fs`**: `FileSystemRepository` hashes as `ref.type` at all four sites (get, put, boot scan, watcher).

Landing: the dispatch named `canonicalize.ts` and the `hashSpec` call site, and measurement kept it there. The type has to reach `canonicalize`, so the two other repository implementations that call `hashSpec` (`InMemoryRepository`, `FileSystemRepository`) pass it too. Otherwise the shared repository contract would hold two hash rules. No `packages/spec/src/**` edit: the order is already declared in spec prose (H2), and the table implements that declaration.

`@objectstack/metadata-core` is graded `minor`: two exports widen (a new optional parameter and a new function). That follows the "WHICH LEVEL" rule in `pr-automation.yml`, under which a fix that widens an index is `minor`. Because the diff widens that published surface, the declaration is `Clause-②: yes`. The claim predicted `no` before the diff existed, and the seat's review corrected it. No payload key, accepted value or error code moves. `metadata-protocol` and `metadata-fs` are `patch`.

## H1: every place a content hash or stored checksum decides "unchanged" (at `18c2ddc1ec`)

| site | compares | what equality drops |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts:620` (`put`) | stored `checksum` vs `hashSpec(incoming)` | the row write, the history row and the watch event; it re-yields the stored item. **The defect site.** |
| `sys-metadata-repository.ts:886` / `:972` (`promoteDraft`) | delegates to `put` above with `parentVersion` = the stored active stamp | the publish (through `:620`); the draft drain still runs, which is why "the draft is gone" |
| `sys-metadata-repository.ts:613` / `:786` (`put` / `delete` lock) | caller `parentVersion` vs stored `checksum` | nothing; inequality throws `ConflictError` (a lock, not a no-op) |
| `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1945` (`rowToItem`) | none; re-derives only when `checksum` is null | n/a (the read returns the stored stamp) |
| `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts:16901` (`storedParentForToken`) | caller `If-Match` token vs keyed digest of the stored head | nothing; inequality answers 409 |
| `protocol.ts:14082` (`getMetaItem` ETag) | `simpleHash` of the served JSON (order-sensitive already) vs `If-None-Match` | the body (304); not a write decision |
| `metadata-core/src/in-memory-repository.ts:107` (`put`) | current head hash vs `hashSpec(incoming)` | the write and the event |
| `metadata-fs/src/repository.ts:362` (`put`) / `:1006` (watcher) | head index (re-derived at boot) vs `hashSpec(body)` | the file write / the external-change event |
| `metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts:1414` (`save`) / `:728` (history) | its own key-sorted `calculateChecksum`, a separate vocabulary | the write / the history row. Reached only through `MetadataManager.register` / `save`; the Studio save and publish path does not call them (no caller of `MetadataManager.register` in `packages/*/src`). Unchanged; see Acceptance notes. |
| `objectql` | `src/` has no comparison. `scripts/dry-run-hash-compat.ts` compares stored `checksum` with type-blind `hashSpec(body)` in an offline audit probe | nothing; it reports. Unchanged; see Acceptance notes. |

## H2: maps a stored metadata body declares ordered

| map | declared ordered? | in the table |
|---|---|---|
| `object.fields` | **yes**. `ObjectFieldGroupSchema` (`data/object.zod.ts` ~1080-1084): "the in-group display order equals the traversal order of `ObjectSchema.fields`", and ungrouped fields keep "their field declaration order". `fieldGroups` (~2090-2093): fields are displayed "in their `ObjectSchema.fields` declaration order". The `record` field type it is authored through (`data/field.zod.ts:90`, `object.form.ts:114`): "Insertion order = display order". `data/display-name.ts:50`: declaration order is `Object.keys` order, and the first title-eligible field "by declaration order" is picked | yes |
| `object.listViews` | no order statement (rendered as tabs, keyed by view name) | no |
| `ObjectExtension.fields` | no statement, and not a stored metadata type (code-only `defineObjectExtension`) | no |
| nested `fields` records (`security/permission.zod.ts:877`, `system/translation.zod.ts:96/206`, flow node configs) | no statement | no |
| inline locale maps (`I18nLabel`) | the resolver breaks ties by key insertion order (`ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts:44`, limbs 3 and 6, mirroring objectui's `pickLocalized`). That is a tie-break rule, not a declared authoring order, and these maps sit at arbitrary depths | no (raised in the report) |
| `AnalyticsQuery.order` / `DatasetSelection.order` | declared ("applied by key in insertion order"), but these are request bodies, not stored metadata. Reports store `order` as an array because "JSON object key order is not a contract" (`ui/report.zod.ts:48`) | n/a |

The only row is `object.fields`, which the spec already declares. No new spec declaration was needed.

## H3: where the order is kept

`canonicalize` takes the metadata type. That is the least surface that keeps one hash rule. A pre-pass in `hashSpec`'s caller would leave `hashSpec(body)` disagreeing with the repository's hash, which breaks contract invariant 4, and every repository implementation would need its own copy. The type is in hand at every call site (`ref.type`), and an omitted type is exactly the old rule. Guarantees 5 (idempotence) and 7 (serialized-form identity, #7856) hold for an ordered map because `JSON.stringify` writes own keys in `Object.keys` order and `JSON.parse` recreates them in that order. Both are pinned as properties under the `object` type.

## H4: stored hashes after the change (measured)

- **Does a stored checksum stop matching the recomputed hash?** Yes, for an object whose `fields` are not in sorted key order. Objects with sorted `fields` hash byte-identically (pinned).
- **Read / ETag / If-Match / conflict:** unaffected. `rowToItem` returns the stored stamp. The ETag hashes the served document, not the checksum. `If-Match` tokens are keyed digests of the stored stamp, and the repository lock compares against the stored stamp. Nothing re-derives a stamp to judge a lock, so upgrading raises no conflict. Pinned end to end: a receipt token taken over a row with an old stamp is honoured by `If-Match`.
- **Misfire 1 (handled):** with only the type-aware hash, an identical re-save of an old row would compare current hash against old stamp, see a difference, and write a history row recording no change. `storedBodyUnchanged` re-hashes the stored bytes under the current rule. The save is a no-op, and the stamp stays as written.
- **Misfire 2 (handled):** a reorder into sorted key order hashes, under the current rule, to exactly the old order-blind stamp. A stamp comparison therefore drops it: the original defect, surviving on exactly the rows stored before the fix. The content comparison writes it.
- **Boot re-derivation:** `SysMetadataRepository` re-derives nothing. `FileSystemRepository` re-derives its head index at boot under the new rule, and the watcher and resync compare new against new, so there are no spurious events. Its JSONL log keeps pre-change hashes, so provenance on `get` / `list` for such an object falls back to defaults until the item next changes. That is measured but not handled; see Acceptance notes.

## H5: the negative

Pinned: swapping the keys around `fields`, the keys inside a field definition, and a map inside a field definition all hash equal under `object`. A property test holds every non-`fields` key order-independent. A `fields` map under a type with no row (`view`), and under no type, hashes equal across a reorder.

## Pins

1. **Dogfood** (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/object-designer-field-reorder.dogfood.test.ts`, showcase, real HTTP). It creates and publishes an object, saves a reorder as a draft, publishes it, and reads the new order back through `GET /api/v1/meta/object/:name` twice (the designer reload), plus the stored row. Then it rewinds the row to the order-blind stamp. An identical save records no history row and keeps the stamp. That save's receipt token is honoured by `If-Match`, and a reorder into sorted order is published.
2. **Hash** (`packages/metadata-core/test/canonicalize.test.ts`): the order half and the unordered half (H5), side by side.
3. **Guarantees 5 and 7** with the ordered map: properties under `object`, plus `toJSON` inside `fields` and on `fields` itself.
4. **H4 at the repository** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.contract.test.ts`, on that file's existing engine double; no new double). The draft-and-publish reorder through `promoteDraft`. Over an old-stamp row: read, identical re-save, draft-and-publish reorder (`previous_checksum` = the old stamp), and the reorder into sorted order.

## Reverse verification (both run from committed state; every mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, `dist/` proven with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`)

**A. Order-blind `fields` restored** (the `object` row deleted from the table). Pre-mutation `dist/` reading: marker `Object.freeze(["fields"])` present in 2 files. Mutate: anchor 1 to 0, blob `c2483ce615dd` to `169e16f653bf`. `metadata-core` rebuilt, preflight `--absent` green.
- pin 2: **5 red / 38 green**. Red: the table row, "hashes a reordered `fields` map differently", "keeps the declared field order", "a reorder INTO sorted order is still a change", and the `toJSON`-on-`fields` case (it asserts the kept order). Green: every H5 case, both byte-identical cases, and both guarantee properties.
- pin 1: **3 red / 2 green**. The reorder publish reads back `title, amount, due`, the card's defect. The stale-stamp precondition and the sorted-order publish are also red. The declared-order create and the identical save stay green.
- pin 4: **5 red / 50 green** (every order-dependent case).
- Restore: blob back to `c2483ce615dd`, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, marker present again, tree clean.

**B. Content comparison reverted to a stamp comparison** (`storedBodyUnchanged`), with the type-aware hash kept. Mutate: anchor 1 to 0, plant 0 to 1, blob `013ffb59ed3d` to `195cf07493ae`.
- pin 4: **2 red / 53 green**. Exactly "an identical re-save: no conflict, no history row" and "a reorder INTO sorted order is written".
- pin 1, after `metadata-protocol` was rebuilt: **1 red / 4 green** ("an identical save records no change"). The type-check of the deliberately ill-typed mutation failed the d.ts step after the JS was emitted, and preflight proved the marker in 2 built JS files.
- Restore: blob back to `013ffb59ed3d`, `git diff HEAD` empty, rebuilt, marker absent, tree clean.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not changed, observed:** `DatabaseLoader` (`packages/metadata`) keeps its own key-sorted `calculateChecksum` and skips a save on equality. It is a second hash vocabulary over the same `sys_metadata` table. It is reached only through `MetadataManager.register` / `save`, which no Studio save or publish path calls (no caller in `packages/*/src`). Carrier: none.
- **Not changed, observed:** the offline probe `packages/objectql/scripts/dry-run-hash-compat.ts` (PR-10d.1) hashes type-blind. On an object row stamped by the new rule with unsorted `fields`, its `checksum_drift` arm fires. It is not published (`files` is `dist` only) and has no runner beyond its own test. Carrier: none.
- **Measured, not handled:** `FileSystemRepository`'s JSONL log keeps pre-change hashes. For an object with unsorted `fields`, provenance on `get` / `list` falls back to defaults: no parent hash, seq `0`, the filesystem actor and the epoch timestamp. This lasts until the item next changes. Production consumer census: `MetadataManager.getRepository()` has no caller in `packages/*/src`, and the manager consumes only `watch()` events, which are unaffected. Stated in the `metadata-fs` changeset.
- **Residue, filed as #21821:** `revertCommit`'s restore limb passes the commit item's stored type to `put` unfolded, so a legacy row stored under a manifest plural such as `objects` reaches the repository under that spelling. The ordered-`fields` rule applies only to the canonical `object` spelling. A reorder-only restore of such a row is therefore skipped as unchanged. Only rows written before the #4432 boundary fold are affected; every `/meta` door folds today.
- `FileSystemRepository` takes the metadata type from the directory name verbatim (`parseItemPath`, no validation). An `objects/` directory would hash order-blind. Its `put` has no production caller; it is attached only as an event source.
- **Carried over from this thread.** The seat's REWORK (comment 5988361846): the declaration is corrected to `Clause-②: yes` here and in the three changesets, and the plural-spelling measurement it asked for is answered in the os-dev-report on #21790. The docs drift check (comment 5988314939): `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx:149` says the hash is a sorted-keys serialization of the body. After this PR that is true except for `object.fields`, whose order is kept. Done at `046c425d62`: that paragraph now says the canonical form sorts keys except in the maps the spec declares ordered (today an `object`'s `fields`), that `put()` still short-circuits on an unchanged body, and that a row written before this release keeps its stored hash as its version token until its content next changes. `dispatch-gates --commands` for that path derives 41 gates. All 41 exit 0, `check:doc-authoring` included, and `--ran` reconciles 41 derived, 41 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. `check:skill-examples` first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET because `client-react` was unbuilt; it passed once that package was built. `origin/main` moved to `ba57588665` (service-settings and the spec crypto-provider contract) after the pre-push check, so this head does not merge it.
- A reorder into sorted order over an old-stamp row is written with `checksum` equal to its `previous_checksum`: the two hashes are taken under different rules. `getByHash` on that value can find either history row. Objects are not `executionPinned`, so no pinned execution resolves through it.
